heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro—advanced foundation models built for professional visual content creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a full-bleed orange hero with a premium mesh gradient and subtle noise texture, then place a layered media cluster on the right half rather than a standard split. The composition should feel editorial and high-end: one large cinematic video thumbnail at the top, a still AI image tile below, and a smaller sync-preview player overlapping them with soft shadows and white UI shells. Keep the left side clean for bold typography at 60px+ H1 scale, with an accent-orange primary CTA and a white secondary CTA. Add floating capability chips around the media stack to signal multimodal power. The hero should feel like a curated creative suite, not a generic SaaS banner.

repetitionBreakers: Hero is full-bleed and visual-first, not text-led
Trust appears immediately after hero as a compact proof strip
Product sections alternate between editorial text bands and preview-led cards
Seedream uses spotlight-plus-grid while Seedance shifts to split-panel or accordion-with-visual to avoid pattern reuse
Testimonials switch to carousel because there are 4+ quotes
Pricing is kept later and presented as a clean comparison-card moment instead of a generic table
Form becomes a strong closing conversion block with a different visual weight than the hero
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image and Video Generation for Teams
blueprint.metaDescription: Create high-quality AI images and videos with ByteDance generative models. Explore Seedream 4.5 for image generation and Seedance 1.5 Pro for synchronized audio-video creation.

sections.backgroundTreatment: solid brand orange with subtle abstract-shape overlays and soft depth layering
sections.designNote: Use a dynamic, visual-first hero with a layered composite: a large AI image preview, a cinematic video frame, small capability chips, and concise headline copy. Keep the text compact and premium, but let the product visuals dominate above the fold to signal creative power immediately.

Since there are no logos or formal badges, convert trust into a compact credibility strip using role-based proof cues and capability statements rather than empty brand badges. Keep it restrained and immediately after the hero to stabilize the high-energy opening.

Start with Seedream 4.5 as a premium spotlight section, using a preview panel plus a dense feature grid because it has 5+ capabilities. Then shift Seedance 1.5 Pro into a contrasting split-panel or accordion-with-visual layout so the rhythm changes and the page does not feel repetitive. Keep the image product first, then move into the motion/video product for a clear narrative progression from static to dynamic creation.

If included, use this as a brief editorial credibility interlude rather than a sales pitch. The section should feel like a clean supporting note with 3 to 4 compact cards emphasizing evaluation support, procurement ease, and enterprise readiness. Avoid making it visually heavy so the main product story remains dominant.

Present pricing late as a conversion-ready comparison moment, with Seedance 1.5 Pro visually emphasized because it has a defined starting price. Keep Seedream as a quote-based enterprise option. This should feel like a decisive commercial checkpoint, not a generic pricing table.

Use a testimonial carousel because there are more than four quotes. Make the quotes role-specific and professionally grounded, rotating between creative director, art director, video producer, marketing manager, and creative lead to reinforce buyer relevance.

Close with a strong lead-capture card that feels polished and low-friction. Keep the form centered with a confident CTA, minimal fields, and a high-contrast card surface so it reads as the final conversion step rather than a utility afterthought.
No news or logos are provided, so this should either be omitted or repurposed as a quiet footer utility zone. Do not force a marquee unless actual media or partner marks are available.

blueprint.designPersonality: An editorial, creator-first AI landing page with confident orange branding, sharp white space, and premium product storytelling. It should feel like a curated creative suite for professionals: structured, high-end, visually intelligent, and distinctly different from dark cinematic AI templates.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use premium editorial composites: a bold orange hero with a layered visual preview showing AI-generated imagery, a cinematic video frame, floating capability chips, and small product UI shells. The gallery must include video content and one image: two video thumbnails or players alongside one still image tile. Use a polished studio feel rather than sci-fi neon, with subtle depth, soft shadows, and motion cues.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long and needs strong hierarchy without crowding; 48px keeps it polished and readable on a premium editorial layout.

colours.colourReason: Brand data is explicit: use Techjockey orange as the primary brand color, with white and charcoal as the supporting base. Orange becomes the hero background and primary CTA color, while white cards and soft grey sections create contrast and premium editorial breathing room.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Full-width top banner with brand/logo lockup, large centered headline, short supporting paragraph, and bullet-based benefit summary; hero is text-led rather than media-led.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single-column narrative flow with a prominent hero followed by a lead-capture form, then stacked content sections; each block uses strong vertical separation and clear hierarchy.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Utility-first content card with solid background, simple border/shadow treatment, compact headings, and dense explanatory copy; prioritizes readability over decoration.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA placed in hero and repeated in section-specific blocks; action language is direct and conversion-focused, while secondary CTAs are minimal or absent.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing section present in the reference structure.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer not visible in the provided reference; pattern should be treated as absent/undetermined.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Minimal media usage in the visible structure; logo mark in hero and no dominant product imagery, suggesting a text-heavy presentation with optional media in later sections.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Stacked feature sections with a section label, title, descriptive paragraph, and list of capability points; follows progressive disclosure from overview to detailed benefits.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form block immediately after hero, using a card container, headline, and hidden metadata fields; designed for conversion capture with low-friction input structure.
referenceMap.animationStyle: No explicit animation pattern is evident in the provided markup; interaction should remain lightweight and static by default.
designNotes: Use a conversion-first landing page structure with strong top-of-page clarity and immediate capture opportunity.
Keep typography hierarchy bold and concise in hero, then transition to denser explanatory sections below.
Prefer simple, reusable content blocks without relying on carousels, tabs, or heavy motion.
Maintain generous whitespace between major sections to preserve the premium B2B feel.
If media is introduced, keep it secondary to copy and aligned to the right or within a contained panel.

blueprint.additionalInstructions: add a gallery in the page containing videos one with image

mustHaveMoments: Hero with clear category positioning for AI image + video generation
Concise benefit-led value proposition tied to ByteDance models
Prominent primary CTA for demo or quote request
Side-by-side product differentiation between Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro
Gallery section featuring video examples and one image example to showcase output quality
Use-case and capability blocks for creative, marketing, and production teams
Pricing/quote section to qualify enterprise buyers
Testimonial block with role-based proof from creative and marketing stakeholders
Final conversion block with repeated CTA and summary of outcomes
avoidPatterns: Long abstract brand storytelling before product value is clear
Heavy trust-badge dependence without proof content
Minimal-media layouts that fail to show generated outputs
Generic feature lists without concrete creative use cases
Landing page structures that feel like a blog article rather than a conversion page
designStrategy.reasoning: This page is aimed at professional buyers who are already aware of generative AI and are evaluating capabilities for real creative workflows, so the page should move quickly from positioning to proof and then to a demo-oriented conversion. Because the offering combines image and video generation, the strongest strategy is product-led with testimonial support, showing output quality early and often. The additional gallery requirement is important: visual evidence will outperform abstract explanation for this audience, especially when one of the products is video-first. A split hero is best because it can immediately communicate the two-model structure while keeping the primary message clear. The overall design should feel dense and enterprise-ready, with strong CTA repetition, direct utility-focused copy, and visual proof of quality rather than a lightweight inspirational brand page.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
